introduction: Illinois EITC is a state tax credit for qualifying workers. Its expanded rules can include some taxpayers who cannot claim the federal EITC.
description: Illinois EITC is a state tax credit for qualifying workers. Its expanded rules can include some taxpayers who cannot claim the federal EITC.

sections.who: For tax year 2025, Illinois includes eligible ITIN filers and eligible adults age 18 or older without qualifying children. Income, identification, filing and other rules still apply; federal ineligibility is not an automatic bar to the expanded state credit.
sections.get: The credit reduces tax and can result in a refund. An additional child tax credit can apply to qualifying Illinois EITC claimants with a child younger than 12 for 2025.
sections.docs:
• Income and investment records for the claim year.
  • Taxpayer and qualifying-child SSN or ITIN information.
  • The federal return and Illinois IL-1040.
  • Schedule IL-E/EITC and any expanded-credit worksheet required.
sections.apply:
1. Check the correct pathway

    Use the Illinois qualification rules.

  2. Calculate the credit

    Complete Schedule IL-E/EITC. Expanded-credit claimants may need its separate worksheet.

  3. File the state return

    Follow the claim-year instructions for carrying the credit to IL-1040.
sections.after: Keep the worksheet and supporting records. Reply to any IDOR request using the instructions in its notice.
sections.sources: Reviewed October 1, 2026 using Illinois EITC overview, 2025 qualifications, claiming instructions. The administering organization decides eligibility.

faqs: Must I qualify for federal EITC?
Not always. Illinois has expanded age and ITIN pathways with other conditions.
Can a child have an ITIN?
Illinois’s 2025 guidance allows a qualifying child to have an SSN or ITIN.
What if I owe no state tax?
The state says to file a return to claim the credit even if no tax is owed.
Schedule IL-E/EITC; follow the state’s separate federal and expanded-credit instructions.
